full_judgment:
2. Facts in short are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed, above case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of 15 decimals land appertaining to RS, khatian Nos. 376 and 377 as mentioned in the schedule of the petition. 

 4. Opposite party No. 1- contested the case by filing, a written objection alleging that the case is a premature one since it was filed before registration of the impugned kobla deed under section 60 of the Registration Act, 1925 and the case is also barred by limitation. The petitioner had orally exchanged his land in the disputed joma with Vadu who is in possession of the same. It was further stated that opposite party No. 2 approached the petitioner to purchase the disputed' land who refused to purchase and the petitioner and his brother had knowledge about the impugned transfer. So the case is barred by the principle of waiver and acquiesce.
